transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-11
Time: 09:00 - 09:57 PT
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen, Diego Morales, Samir Patel, Lena Hoffman, Maya Rivera, Jon Park, Priya Nair, Tom Wu, Eleanor Briggs, Carlos Mendes, Ravi Shah

[00:00] Ava Chen: alright good morning everyone thanks for joining. uh quick agenda — q2 launch readiness checklist, dedicated capacity validation, brief incident review from last week, and security outstanding items. we'll keep this tight, 45-ish minutes then open q&a.

[00:22] Diego Morales: sounds good. real quick, we have two main gating items for launch — Dedicated capacity perf and the rollout playbook + rollback. I ran a quick smoke with the new kernel selection and we saw latency variance at 2k tokens, so we need to validate again with the production load profile.

[00:39] Samir Patel: yeah the autoscale flapping on March 3rd exposed a timing issue between the scale decisions and KV cache warmup. cache cold starts were causing 2x token costs in the spike window.

[00:55] Priya Nair: are we confident that the UX fallbacks are in place? like, when we route to smaller quantized models does the assistant degrade gracefully? I want to avoid abrupt output regressions.

[01:10] Diego Morales: good point — we have the fallback policy implemented but we haven't run a graceful-degrade eval against our core prompts. Carlos, can you run the regression set?

[01:20] Carlos Mendes: yes, I'll queue the evals today. expect first pass results by Thursday. note: quantization does change some tokens so we'll include quality thresholds.

[01:35] Lena Hoffman: on the launch checklist side, we still need sign-off on observability retention tiers — marketing wants 90 days for per-route traces but infra is worried about cost.

[01:48] Tom Wu: cost is the tradeoff — if we keep 90 days at full fidelity it's expensive. we proposed token-level sampling for older traces which cuts cost by ~60% in our estimate.

[02:05] Ava Chen: okay sample approach sounds reasonable, let's put that in the checklist as option A and a reduced-fidelity option B.

[02:20] Samir Patel: back to the incident — root cause appears to be the autoscaler decision loop hitting a state where instances were removed before KV caches were fully populated. that caused a cascade of cold-starts and higher latency which triggered more scaling.

[02:40] Diego Morales: yeah, basically a feedback loop. Proposed fix: add a short grace period before removing nodes and introduce warmup jobs to prefill KV cache on spin-up. Maya, can you check the warmup script and move it to CI?

[02:55] Maya Rivera: on it, I'll validate the script tonight and add a smoke test. also I'll add metrics to flag if warmup didn't reach threshold within N seconds.

[03:10] Jon Park: QA to add a chaos test that simulates node churn and verifies fallback routing. we caught a few edge cases in the last run.

[03:25] Ava Chen: perfect. security — Ravi? last time you had a note about SAML flows for the Private deployment and KMS/HSM cert rotation.

[03:35] Ravi Shah: yes. SOC2 scope update is in flight. for Private/VPC we need to confirm HSM integration for key rotation plus audit logs retention policy. I still need confirmation on whether the on-prem package will support our HSM shim; ops said yes but I'd like a written confirmation.

[03:55] Eleanor Briggs: support readiness — we need runbooks for rollback and for customer-facing incident comms. who will own the comms template?

[04:05] Lena Hoffman: Product ops will own the comms template; support will own the exec notification list. we'll coordinate and put in the checklist.

[04:20] Ava Chen: timeline recap: we want a dry-run for the deployment on 2026-03-22, can we hit that?

[04:30] Diego Morales: tight but possible if perf validation and warmup CI are done this week. Dedicated capacity numbers need to be in by 2026-03-18 so procurement can reserve the vGPU pool.

[04:44] Samir Patel: also need to confirm autoscaler config does not conflict with burst policies — we saw conflicting policies where the system would auto-burst then scale down too fast.

[04:58] Ava Chen: okay action items then — we assigned owners. please make sure to update the shared launch doc and I'll do an exec summary on Monday.

[05:12] Carlos Mendes: small note — when we benchmark against Anthropic/OpenAI numbers, remember we're comparing different endpoint semantics; we'll present normalized throughput and p95 latency.

[05:28] Priya Nair: design asks: we should include graceful messaging when we degrade models, and UX copy to set expectations for slight hallucination increase if we go to a quantized fallback.

[05:45] Diego Morales: agreed, include that in the canary playbook.

[06:00] Ava Chen: any blockers we haven't captured?

[06:05] Ravi Shah: one ask — legal needs a list of third party libs used for the quantization path for the compliance review.

[06:15] Tom Wu: I'll export the dependency list and share with legal today.

[06:25] Jon Park: QA will plan the chaos test and assign smoke test owners.

[06:35] Lena Hoffman: I'll compile the launch checklist, add the observability options, and circulate Friday.

[06:48] Ava Chen: great. recap — deliverables: checklist (Lena/Ava), Dedicated perf numbers (Diego), warmup->CI + metrics (Maya), incident PM (Samir), SOC2/KMS updates (Ravi), UX copy for degrade (Priya), legal deps (Tom), chaos/QA plan (Jon). dry-run target 2026-03-22.

[07:12] Diego Morales: one last bit — let's include a short runbook for cost mitigation: token sampling, prefix cache heuristics, and automatic quantized routing thresholds. I'll draft a page in the launch doc.

[07:30] Ava Chen: awesome. thanks everyone. I'll follow up with the exec summary and send calendar invites for the dry-run. meeting adjourned.

[57:00] End of recording.
